_what: Curated NEPRA plant-name -> canonical plant -> listed PSX operator crosswalk. Reviewable data, not runtime inference.
_provenance: Canonical names and aliases are the VERBATIM 'Name of Companies' cells of the NEPRA generation workbooks for FY2017-18 and FY2023-24 (cp1252-decoded, fetched 2026-09-08); see testdata/published_names.json for the raw column. parent_name / psx_ticker / confidence / evidence are hand-curated: every PSX symbol was confirmed against https://dps.psx.com.pk/company/<SYMBOL> on 2026-09-08.

_field_semantics.canonical_name: Whitespace-normalised form of the name published in the LATEST fiscal year in which the plant appears. Case and trailing punctuation are preserved as published.
_field_semantics.aliases: Every DISTINCT raw published string seen for this plant, verbatim, including U+00A0 NBSP padding and the newline+indent Excel's HTML export inserts. Resolve() indexes all of them.
_field_semantics.parent_name: Empty string means NO parent is asserted (unknown). It never means 'no parent exists'.
_field_semantics.psx_ticker: Empty string means NO ticker is asserted. Read listed_status to tell 'not listed on PSX' apart from 'listing unknown'.
_field_semantics.listed_status: listed | not_listed | unknown. 'unknown' is a real state and must not be collapsed to 'not_listed'.
_field_semantics.valid_from_fy: FIRST fiscal year in which this identity was OBSERVED in a fetched workbook. It is NOT a commissioning date: only FY2017-18 and FY2023-24 were fetched, so a valid_from_fy of 2023-24 means 'not in the FY2017-18 workbook', not 'did not exist before'.
_field_semantics.valid_to_fy: Empty string means the identity is still published in the latest observed fiscal year (2023-24), i.e. an OPEN interval. A non-empty value is the last fiscal year in which it was observed. IT IS A PUBLICATION INTERVAL, NOT AN OPERATING CLAIM: all 133 rows have an empty valid_to_fy, including the 13 FY2023-24 plants whose monthly block reads DELICENSED or DECOMMISSIONED. Read observed[].block_status for operating status.
_field_semantics.confidence: high | medium | low | unattributed - describes the parent_name/psx_ticker attribution only, NOT the plant identity. Plant identity is always high: it is a verbatim published string.
_field_semantics.evidence: Free text. Always starts with the workbook provenance (fiscal year, S.No, published installed capacity), then the parent research.
_field_semantics.observed: Per-fiscal-year appearance: S.No, the published name that year, technology, fuel, the installed-capacity string EXACTLY as published, the state of that capacity cell, and the status of the plant's MONTHLY GENERATION BLOCK. An empty installed_capacity_mw_raw means the workbook cell was blank or NBSP-only - NOT REPORTED, never zero.
_field_semantics.observed.installed_capacity_state: nepraparse's classification of the installed-capacity CELL: numeric | not_reported | export_to_k_electric | delicensed | decommissioned | unknown_text. It is why an unparseable capacity is distinguishable from a blank one. Measured: FY2017-18 has 11 not_reported, FY2020-21 has 3 export_to_k_electric, FY2023-24 has 0 non-numeric.
_field_semantics.observed.block_status: Status of the plant's TWELVE-MONTH GENERATION BLOCK in that fiscal year, as typed by nepraparse: numeric (ordinary data) | delicensed | decommissioned. THIS IS AN OPERATING-STATUS FACT AND IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM COLUMNS 0-4: it lives in the monthly block, which is why the first cut of this file omitted it and presented 13 non-operating FY2023-24 plants (3,880 MW, including the DELICENSED 1,292 MW Hub Power Company) as live capacity. A delicensed or decommissioned plant KEEPS a valid installed capacity, so capacity must never be nulled on account of it - it must be reported separately from operating capacity. Measured over 241 observations: 228 numeric, 12 delicensed, 1 decommissioned, all 13 in FY2023-24.

_held_out: The FY2020-21 workbook was deliberately NOT used to build this crosswalk, so it can serve as an out-of-sample test of the alias table. Measured: 107 of its 108 published names resolve (99.1%), 1 declines. See testdata/heldout_2020-21.json and the possible_duplicates entry for (NPPCL) - Balloki.
sno_is_not_a_key: Of the 107 plant names common to both fetched workbooks (whitespace-normalised), ZERO keep the same S.No: FY2023-24 was re-sorted by technology. Measured examples: AES Lalpir 1->36, Allai Khwar 56->8, Kot Addu (KAPCO) 9->33, Kohinoor (KEL) 12->35, Narowal 11->58. Joining fiscal years on S.No swaps plants' entire histories.

absent_parents.absence_note: K-Electric's OWN generation fleet is not in the NEPRA generation workbooks. Searching the FY2017-18 and FY2023-24 'Name of Companies' columns for BQPS, Korangi, SITE, Bin Qasim, KESC, 'K-Electric' and 'Karachi Electric' returns ZERO rows in either year (241 published names searched). This is a dataset scope limit - these workbooks cover NTDC/CPPA-G-dispatched plants - and NOT a measurement of zero generation. Any generation figure for K-Electric must come from another source.
absent_parents.caveat: The bare token 'KEL' is ambiguous: it is K-Electric's PSX symbol AND NEPRA's acronym for Kohinoor Energy Limited (PSX KOHE), a 131 MW RFO plant that IS in this dataset. PlantsForParent treats its argument as a PSX symbol only; use ResolveTicker for bare tokens and it will refuse.

possible_duplicates.suspicion: NEPRA publishes BOTH rows with the base string 'Foundation Wind Energy-I Ltd.' and distinguishes them only by the parenthetical (FWEL-I) vs (FWEL-II). The second is almost certainly an upstream typo for 'Foundation Wind Energy-II Ltd.'. Both are 50 MW WIND and co-occur in the SAME workbook (FY2017-18 S.No 77/78; FY2023-24 S.No 101/102), so they are two different plants and MUST NOT be merged. This pair is why Resolve() refuses a parenthetical-stripped match whose base form hits more than one row.

Found by holding the FY2020-21 workbook out of this crosswalk and resolving it (testdata/heldout_2020-21.json): 107 of its 108 published names resolved and the single decline was '(NPPCL) - Balloki' (FY2020-21 S.No 30, 1,223 MW).
